Laskod Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · József Attila utca 2, Hungary

Not demolished. Laskod's Orthodox Jewish community maintained only a synagogue and a cemetery, with relationships between Jewish and non-Jewish residents described as good — the town's judge toward the end of WWI, for instance, was Jewish. The population fluctuated from 29 residents in 1848 to a peak of 58 by 1930, before falling to 23 by 1941. Under Romanian occupation beginning in 1920, Jews suffered robberies and other atrocities; in 1941, young Jewish men were taken into forced labor service, and the remaining Jews of Laskod were taken to the Kisvárda Ghetto in 1944 and deported to Auschwitz. Only a few returned after the war; by 1963, none remained in the village. This cemetery, though not marked on an 1870 cadastral map, holds tombstones dating from 1853 to at least 1921.
